options.tagline: Chase sunrises and golden hour — hike the Wall, summit Huangshan, shoot the cities after dark.
options.title: Active + Photography
options.why_suits_you: You're an active hiker who shoots sunrises and viewpoints, and this is the photographer's cut of the trip: a pre-dawn start for sunrise on the Jinshanling Great Wall, Huangshan's West Sea Canyon plus a summit sunrise, a dawn bike loop around West Lake, and blue-hour shoots in Wuzhen and Hong Kong. The big hiking days are real workouts with real payoffs, and your dad can set his own pace on each — everything is planned around first and last light, with midday downtime built in.

options.tagline: Temples, museums, opera, and tea — the 5,000-year version of the trip.
options.title: Culture Deep-Dive
options.why_suits_you: You like knowing the story behind what you're seeing, and this route trades a packed checklist for depth: the Forbidden City with a licensed guide, Peking opera in a theater built for it, a gongfu tea ceremony in a Longjing farmhouse, and Wuzhen's night performance. The pace is deliberately unhurried — fewer miles, longer conversations — which suits traveling with your dad and actually absorbing 5,000 years instead of sprinting past it.

activities.name: In-town check-in, then the Tung Chung Line
activities.detail: Free Conrad shuttle at 8:00 AM to Hong Kong Station. Cathay in-town check-in (6:00 AM–11:00 PM): check the suitcases through to JFK and collect boarding passes — the Airport Express fare (HK$120 each, tapped on the Octopus) is the price of the service; you then ride the Tung Chung Line, bags-free. Tung Chung by ~9:10 AM.

activities.name: Ngong Ping 360 + Big Buddha + Po Lin Monastery
activities.detail: Standard cabin round trip on the Klook voucher (both legs today). Up by ~9:45 AM: the Tian Tan Buddha (34 m, 268 steps) and Po Lin Monastery opposite — the compressed flight-day cut: the platform, the Six Devas, the monastery's main axis. No monastery lunch today; lunch is at the airport lounge. Hard deadline: in the down-queue by 12:30 PM.

activities.name: Down, and straight to the airport
activities.detail: Cable car down to Tung Chung (~25 min), then a blue Lantau taxi from the terminal rank (~10 min) or the S1 bus (HK$3.70, ~12 min) to the airport — at HKG by ~1:20–1:35 PM. Refund the Octopus cards at the Airport Express station's customer service centre before security. Lunch airside: The Pier Business (Cathay, near Gate 65) on the business ticket — noodle bar and teahouse; or the Centurion Lounge (Gate 60) / Kyra Lounge (Gate 23, Priority Pass). CX840 boards ~3:50 PM.

meals.detail: On the business ticket, Cathay's own lounges are the top tier for lunch: The Pier Business (near Gate 65 — the noodle bar, the Teahouse, à la carte dishes; the lunch pick) or The Wing Business (near Gates 1–3) if your gate is low. The Amex / Priority Pass pair behind them: The Centurion Lounge (Level 7 near Gate 60 — best bar, showers; a guest fee may apply for the second traveller) and Kyra Lounge (near Gate 23, Priority Pass — guests included). Pick by the gate on your boarding pass.

options.tagline: Eat your way across China — duck, dim sum, tea, and night markets.
options.title: Food-First
options.why_suits_you: You're a foodie traveling with your dad, and this route is a greatest-hits of Chinese regional cooking: Beijing roast duck and imperial snacks, Huizhou's stinky mandarin fish, Hangzhou's delicate lake cuisine, Macanese egg tarts, and Hong Kong dim sum. Every day is built around one anchor meal worth planning for, with reservations flagged where the famous spots book out — and the eating is paced so the hiking days still work.
